title: st edit hands back the path to a generated view and the next render destroys the edit, where the published tag refused
body:
**`intent st edit <id> info` hands back the path to a generated view, and the next render destroys what you write there. The published tag refuses the same command.**

Driven on the tree binary `intent 3.0.0 (a854d7c3)`, in a project that binary created:

    $ intent st edit ST0001 info
    <path>/intent/st/ST0001/info.md          rc=0
    $ printf 'OPERATOR-AUTHORED-SENTINEL-9f3c\n' >> <path>/intent/st/ST0001/info.md
    $ intent sync --to-disk ST0001
    $ grep -c SENTINEL-9f3c <path>/intent/st/ST0001/info.md
    0

**The same command on the published keg `intent 3.0.0 (80d8b2ca)` refuses, and its refusal names this exact consequence:**

    error: `intent/st/ST0001/info.md` is generated from the model, so an edit here is lost at the next render

So the guard existed at the tag and does not fire here. **It has not been deleted** -- the error variant is live at `intentsvcs/src/facade.rs:818`, and it still fires on the sibling: `st edit ST0001 acceptance` refuses with that same text at rc=1. **Both files are generated; only one is guarded.** That inconsistency is the defect, and `info` is the unguarded one -- which is the worse half, because `info` is the register's DEFAULT for the `file` argument, so bare `intent st edit ST0001` reaches it too.

=== WHY THIS IS NOT A DOCS-LAG NOTE ===

Every other divergence found driving `docs/getting-started.md` today runs the safe way: the keg lacks something the tree has, so the docs are ahead and the tag closes the gap. **This one runs the other way.** The page is correct about the published binary and wrong about the build that ships next, and the change it fails to describe replaces a refusal with silent data loss. A reader who follows `docs/getting-started.md:60` on 3.0.1 is told the command refuses, finds that it does not, and reasonably concludes the file is theirs to edit.

=== A CONTRADICTION FOR WHOEVER OWNS THE VERB ===

`intent-cli/tests/st_edit_opens_or_prints.rs` states in its header that this invocation `does not work at HEAD and has not since c4709d3f`, and that it drives its property through `design` instead because that is `a file this verb can actually hand back`. Against `a854d7c3` -- which contains `c4709d3f` -- **both claims are false**: `info` returns a path and `design` refuses. The test file's reasoning and the binary disagree, and the reasoning is what a future reader will trust.

Filed by dc from the AC-02.1 drive; the verb and its test are not mine.
